inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 36,340,747 shares outstanding per Q2-2026 10-Q cover (as of 2026-07-23) plus ~0.05M dilutive awards (Q2-26 diluted 36,132k vs basic 36,085k weighted). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting as well would double-charge. No non-SBC issuance.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow add-back $22.733M (SEC XBRL ShareBasedComp) plus an ESTIMATED ~$3M of tax withheld on net-share settlement: POOL books surrendered shares inside 'Repurchases of common stock' and does not disclose the dollar figure separately (Q2-26 10-Q issuer-purchases table: 16k shares surrendered in May 2026). No combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC figure is published.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Cost of equity ~9.6% (10y UST ~4.3% + beta ~1.05 x 5.0% ERP); after-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (SOFR-based revolver/receivables facility + swaps, 25% tax); market-value weights ~81% equity ($5.85bn) / 19% debt ($1.34bn) -> ~8.6%, used 8.5%. Same WACC in every scenario: cyclicality is charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842 operating leases: lease cost (FY25 $114.2M) is already inside SG&A and therefore inside EBITDA and the flows. Operating lease liabilities ($354.5M at 2026-06-30) are EXCLUDED from net debt. One treatment (leases as operating cost); lease_cost_pct_path = 0 because the charge is already in the margin.
inputs.nci_treatment: None: wholly-owned subsidiaries, no non-controlling interest.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, cyclical mid-cycle variant (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, cyclical'; owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Pool Corp is a wholesale distributor with ~60% non-discretionary maintenance revenue and ~40% rate-sensitive new construction/remodel; FY20-22 was a COVID boom (EBIT margin peaked 16.6% FY22, EPS $18.89) and FY23-25 a normalisation (EBIT margin 11.0% FY25, near the FY19 pre-COVID 10.7%). Reported FCF swings with inventory (FY23 $828M on a $231M inventory release, FY25 $310M on a $147M build), so the base is NOT the latest FCF: margins are built from components and steered toward a mid-cycle EBIT margin of ~11.5% (base), between the pre-COVID 9-11% trend and the 15-17% peak. ANCHORS: price 2026-10-01 close; total debt $1,340.7M (13.4 current + 1,327.3 long-term) and cash $28.8M from the Q2-2026 10-Q balance sheet (2026-06-30) -- the latest filing; SEC companyfacts still stopped at Q1-26 so these were read from the 10-Q itself. June is the seasonal working-capital peak (receivables +$292M in H1), so net debt is ~$200M above the December level; because FY2026 is modelled as a full year the H1-26 seasonal outflow (~-$54M owner FCF) is counted in both net debt and Y1 flows -- a ~$1.5/share conservative bias, accepted to keep the latest-balance-sheet rule. FY2026 guidance (Q2-26 10-Q, 2026-07-29): GAAP diluted EPS $10.66-10.96, adjusted $10.87-11.17 excluding ~$0.21 CEO-transition costs; low-single-digit sales growth mostly price (2-3%); gross margin ~30bp below FY25. Base Y1 is built to that: 3% growth, 12.1% pre-SBC EBITDA margin (FY25 12.36%: EBIT 580.2 + D&A 51.4 + SBC 22.7), which yields NOPAT ~$435M, consistent with ~$400M guided net income plus ~$53M after-tax-adjusted interest. BUYBACKS: an active repurchaser ($346M FY25, $86M H1-26, $600M authorisation) so the flat share count is funded, not just a convention. WORKING CAPITAL: distributor with inventory + receivables (~$1.8bn at Dec-25) far above payables, so wc_capture is NEGATIVE (-25% of the revenue increase, ~ net working capital / sales). INTEREST INCOME: none stripped -- the company is net debt. HISTORICAL CAGRs: equity CAGR is distorted by ~$1.4bn of buybacks FY22-25 and is not used; revenue 5yr CAGR (6.1%, includes the COVID step-up) is the reference, and the base path averages ~4.5%.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 13.1% vs EPS 5yr 3.6% and revenue 5yr 6.1% (>30% divergence): equity is shaped by buybacks (~$1.4bn FY22-25) and the FY20-22 boom, not by compounding. All 3yr CAGRs are negative because FY2022 is the cyclical peak. Owner-FCF CAGRs (on FCF less SBC) run ~0.6-1.2pp below reported FCF CAGRs -- SBC grew from $14.5M to $22.7M while FCF fell -- but SBC is only ~0.4% of sales, so the gap is immaterial. FCF CAGRs are also dominated by inventory swings and should not be read as a trend.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series = reported FCF - SBC (cash-flow add-back): FY2020 $361.4M, FY2022 $426.4M, FY2025 $286.8M. Equity-award withholding not separately disclosed historically and excluded from the CAGR series (immaterial, ~$3M/yr).

base.rationale: FY26 at guidance (3% price-led growth, margin slightly below FY25 on freight/mix and CEO-transition costs). Gradual new-construction and remodel recovery FY27-30 (4.5-6% growth: ~2-3% price, installed-base growth, partial construction rebound from ~50% below peak, building-materials share gains), fading to 3%. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin recovers to 13.0% = ~11.5% EBIT after SBC and D&A: mid-cycle, above FY19's 10.7% on structurally higher gross margin and private-label/POOL360 mix, well below the 16.6% FY22 peak. Capex FY26 elevated (H1 $36.6M vs $27.4M) then ~1.15% of sales vs D&A 1.05%. Cash tax 25% (H1-26 ETR 25.4%; FY24/FY25 cash taxes were distorted by the IRS hurricane-relief deferral, so the GAAP rate is used). Cap 15x: cyclical distributor, lower end of the house range is not warranted for a 35-40% share leader, but Gordon at 8.5%/3% (~18.7x) would grant an exit multiple no buyer has to pay.

bull.rationale: Rate cuts revive financed new-pool construction and big-ticket remodels from FY27 (7-9% growth for three years as construction retraces part of the ~50% decline), operating leverage plus private-label mix lift pre-SBC EBITDA to 14.5% (~13% EBIT, roughly the FY23 level, still below the FY21-22 peak). Exit at 17x reflects the historical premium the market pays for the category leader in a recovery.

bear.rationale: No construction recovery: rates stay high, discretionary stays 'muted' through FY28, and Home Depot-backed Heritage/SRS takes share and forces price investment. Growth is price plus maintenance only (1-3%); gross-margin compression continues (freight, tariffs, mix) and pre-SBC EBITDA settles at 11.5% (~10% EBIT, the FY19 level). Exit at 13x for a slower, more contested distributor.

scenario_narratives.base: The ~60% maintenance base (chemicals, parts, repair on 14m+ ageing US pools) keeps compounding at price plus installed-base growth, while new construction and major remodel -- roughly half their 2022 level -- recover gradually as rates ease rather than snapping back. POOL holds its 35-40% share: Heritage under Home Depot is a real competitor but early share loss is modest, and POOL360/private label (~18% of sales) and building-materials gains offset freight and mix pressure. Margins return to a mid-cycle ~11.5% EBIT, between the pre-COVID trend and the pandemic peak; the new CEO executes a continuity plan (sales excellence, pricing discipline, bolt-on M&A).
scenario_narratives.bull: A rate-cutting cycle unlocks pent-up financed demand: new pool starts and big-ticket remodels (resurfacing, automation, outdoor living) recover meaningfully in FY27-29, operating leverage on a fixed branch network lifts EBIT margin toward 13%, and the consolidation flywheel resumes with bolt-ons. The market re-awards the category leader a premium multiple at exit.
scenario_narratives.bear: The discretionary trough lasts: high mortgage/HELOC rates keep construction depressed, small builder customers fail or retrench, and Home Depot's capital lets Heritage buy independents and compete on price, eroding POOL's share and gross margin. Tariffs and freight squeeze margin further; growth is price-only and EBIT margin settles near FY19's ~10%. The new, first-time CEO's execution and rising leverage (debt-funded buybacks) add to the de-rating.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): a structurally stronger #2 competitor (Heritage/SRS under Home Depot), a CEO transition in a soft market and gross-margin compression in guidance are live, not hypothetical, though maintenance revenue and ~2.6x net debt/EBITDA make this an earnings-trough risk, not a solvency one. Base 50%: the guided, price-led stabilisation followed by gradual normalisation is the central path. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it needs both a rate cycle that revives financed construction and no meaningful share loss, two things outside management's control.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value POOL on mid-cycle owner FCF, not on the boom (FY21-22) or the inventory-distorted latest FCF. Pre-SBC EBITDA margins are steered to a stated mid-cycle level per scenario, working capital consumes cash as revenue grows (distributor), SBC is fully expensed with a flat share count, and cyclicality is priced through the scenario flows and weights at a single 8.5% USD WACC.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value carries most of the value; the 15x cap binds in base (Gordon ~18.7x), so the exit multiple is the key judgment.
Timing of the new-construction recovery: every year it slips pushes the base path toward the bear.
Heritage/SRS (Home Depot) share gains and price competition compressing the gross margin that underpins the mid-cycle margin assumption.
Working-capital intensity: inventory decisions swing annual FCF by $150-250M, so any single year's FCF is a poor anchor.
June balance sheet is the seasonal debt peak; net debt is ~$200M above the December level.
